summary: The paper investigates whether providing an immutable, read-only activation reference improves tracking and restoration performance across sequential board edits in a feed-forward residual network. Through a carefully balanced evaluation protocol and counterfactual activation patching, the author demonstrates that while the model does attend to the reference, freezing it confers no statistically meaningful advantage over a writable reference or standard residual connections.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design that actively identified and corrected an 86.6% shortcut bias in the initial benchmark data.
Transparent reporting of null results, accompanied by paired seed comparisons and 10,000-draw bootstrap confidence intervals.
Use of causal activation patching to empirically verify whether the network actively utilizes the protected activations.
Clear, concise, and objective writing that candidly acknowledges architectural constraints and scope limitations.
weaknesses: No supporting repository artifact was supplied directly with the submission, restricting the evaluation to text-only verification.
Evaluated on a single toy synthetic task (8-square board, 4 colors, 6 edits) with a fixed width of 64, leaving open whether the findings generalize to complex or scaled settings.
Small sample size of training seeds (five seeds), resulting in wide confidence intervals (-1.77 to +1.19 percentage points).
suggestions: Verify the implementation with an open-source artifact containing reproducible test harness scripts and fixed dataset seeds.
Expand the parameter sweep across multiple widths, block depths, and sequence lengths to establish scaling boundaries for the immutable reference inductive bias.
Report exact training convergence curves and compute wall-clock overhead across the four architectural variants.

claims.text: DenseNet established a precedent for forward reuse of earlier features.
Synthetic recall research likewise illustrates the importance of defining what a correct output actually tests.
Activation-patching studies describe how intervention choices affect interpretation.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While DenseNet concatenates all preceding layer representations throughout deep blocks, this benchmark specifically isolates a fixed read-only input reference against writable state tracking across sequential edit operations.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies activation patching methodologies as a diagnostic tool to verify functional reliance on protected intermediate slots within a synthetic board-editing feed-forward network.
